THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner has challenged the Look Out Circular issued by respondent No.3 in Cr.No.46/2020 now pending on the file of VI Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore in C.C.No.14396/2020.
NC: 2023:KHC:33880 2.

entities.text: VI Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioners are sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 5 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

3. The case of the prosecution is that, petitioners/accused subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty who is legally wedded wife of accused No.1 and a demand was made to bring money from parental home.
4. The matter was referred to the Mediation Centre Bangalore to explore the possibility of settlement between the parties.

The parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves Sri Sudhir Gupta vs Commissioner Of Police on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184910956/
4 before the Mediation Centre Bangalore and as per the terms of the settlement, accused No.1 and the defacto complainant have agreed to dissolve their marriage mutually in M.C.No.2465/2022 on the file of I Addl. Principal Judge, Family Court, Bangalore which is pending consideration.
5.

entities.text: Sri Sudhir Gupta vs Commissioner Of Police
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: I Addl. Principal Judge, Family Court, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In terms of the settlement accused No.1 has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.35,00,000/- towards permanent alimony out of which a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- is paid through demand draft and the receipt of which is acknowledged by the defacto complainant who is present before the Court,
subject to realization.

Accused No.1 has undertaken to pay the balance amount of Rs.10,00,000/- to the defacto complainant in M.C.No.2465/2022 and balance amount of Rs.5,00,000/- in the NC:
2023:KHC:33880 petition filed under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act in Crl.Misc.
No.83/2020.
6.
The second respondent who is present before the Court has stated that she has no objection for quashing the LOC as well as the impugned proceedings.

7. Though the offences alleged against the petitioner/accused No.1 are cognizable and non compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves and the defacto complainant having no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if petitioner/accused No.1 is subjected to trial, since the probability of conviction of the petitioner/accused No.1 is remote and bleak.
Accordingly, I pass the following ORDER i.
Petitions are allowed.

ii. The impugned LOC No.2026435171 issued by the Deputy Commissioner of Police, East Division,
Bangalore against petitioner/accused No.1 issued against passport No.Z2974062 issued on 23.09.2014 to the petitioner/accused No.1 stands quashed.
iii. The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.14396/2020 on the file of VI Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore is hereby quashed.
